current_determination: The reflection-adapted soft kernel is structurally compatible with the Bałaban weak-field Gaussian family at quadratic order. Its soft-hard quadratic defect behaves as p^4 and is therefore a dimension-six, tree-level L^-2 irrelevant correction. The nonlinear kernel remainder is not wholly irrelevant: its cubic and quartic pieces can project onto the marginal Yang-Mills F^2 operator. The correct decomposition is a finite coupling-coordinate/scheme shift plus a gauge-invariant dimension-six-and-higher remainder. The unresolved theorem is quantitative closure of that residual local functional in Bałaban's actual analytic/localized polymer norms, including the precise marginal extraction used in his coupling recursion.
major_new_results: The quadratic defect E_a = -a^-1 Delta_infty^2 (I+a^-1 Delta_infty)^-1 begins at p^4 and has canonical dimension six in 4d, hence tree-level scaling gain L^-2.
Cubic/higher field order does not imply irrelevance because tr F^2 itself contains cubic and quartic Yang-Mills vertices.
The soft-kernel nonlinear remainder must be locally projected onto the marginal tr F^2 coordinate before irrelevance can be asserted.
After gauge/reflection symmetry constraints and marginal extraction, the generic residual local pure-gauge operators begin at canonical dimension six.
An analytic finite coupling redefinition changes the RG scheme but preserves the universal first two beta-function coefficients; prior reference [51] remains the scheme-control source.
negative_results: Do not classify all R_{>=3} as irrelevant merely from polynomial field degree.
